# C6 — Spring margin consistency

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **CONTRADICTED** — Current evidence contradicts the claim or one of its requirements. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, ANALYTICAL |

| Last review | CURRENT — snapshot recorded 2026-09-28 by tooling snapshot (no human review) |

**Question.** Does the stated 220 N*m/rad torsion spring exceed the calculated minimum rate by at least 20%?

**Current statement.** At the stated design point the calculated minimum spring rate is 184.9 N*m/rad. The stated 220 N*m/rad spring gives a 19.0% margin, below the stated requirement of at least 20%. No spring has been characterized.

## Assumptions

- The requirement and the reported margin use the same definition: (k_supplied - k_min) / k_min.
- The design point (205 m/s, 120 mm chord, 154 g fin, 50 ms deployment) is the intended one.

## Limitations

- The damping treatment divides by (1 - damping ratio), a heuristic.
- Design-point inputs were revised to match the paper's k_min (D-009).
- No component has been measured.

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- A decision on the requirement or the spring, recorded by a human.
- Inert torque-angle characterization of the supplied spring (proposed pre-registration P-002).
